positions.thesis: AMD received a Citi upgrade to Buy ($575 PT) on June 12 and announced a £2B UK AI infrastructure investment over five years, providing fresh stock-specific catalysts on top of broader AI server CPU demand. Semiconductor sector is recovering from the June 6 AVGO-guidance selloff; multiple Wall Street analysts have lifted AMD targets to $600-665. The Citi upgrade from Neutral represents institutional re-rating momentum.

Vistra is a pure AI-power demand play: its nuclear and gas baseload fleet supplies data-center load growth via long-term PPAs, and analysts rate it Strong Buy with a ~$225 median target. On June 15 VST rose ~4.5% even as oil collapsed to ~$80 on the US-Iran peace deal, confirming the stock trades on electricity/AI demand rather than the oil complex and providing diversification away from my semiconductor exposure. Relative strength on a risk-on day with a structural multi-year tailwind makes this a momentum-plus-thesis entry.

Marvell joins the S&P 500 effective June 22, 2026, forcing index/passive funds to buy the stock ahead of the add date — a mechanical demand catalyst that falls squarely inside this simulation's window. MRVL cleared the profitability hurdle on AI data-center networking strength and is up ~210% YTD. The index-inclusion bid is largely independent of fundamental sector beta and provides near-term support; the primary risk is a 'sell-the-news' reversal on June 22, after this run ends.
